original_question: If X is a Banach space with a norming Markushevich basis and Z is a subspace of X, must Z also admit a norming Markushevich basis?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 6.1: the heredity problem for norming Markushevich bases, namely whether the property of admitting a norming M-basis passes to subspaces. The introduction previews exactly this question as “whether the existence of norming M-bases passes to subspaces.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target very closely: it asks the general heredity question for norming Markushevich bases in Banach spaces, with X having a norming M-basis and Z being a subspace, and it asks for existence of a norming M-basis on Z itself. It also correctly stays at the general-subspace level rather than drifting to the countably norming/Plichko analogue or the separate complemented-subspace variant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, define “norming Markushevich basis”: an M-basis is a fundamental and total biorthogonal system, and it is norming when the linear span of its biorthogonal functionals is a norming subspace of the dual (Definition 2.1, together with the definition of M-basis just above it). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Clarify that Z is being considered as a Banach subspace with the inherited norm; in a fully explicit stand-alone formulation one would normally say “closed linear subspace” so that Z is itself a Banach space. This is an implicit Banach-space convention rather than an extra hypothesis added by the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

Make explicit that the question is about whether Z admits some norming M-basis, not whether the given M-basis of X restricts to one on Z. The paper’s Problem 6.1 is an existence question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

State that no extra assumptions such as separability, WLD, WCG, Asplundness, or complementedness belong to the target problem itself; separability and WLD appear only in positive partial results, and complementedness is treated separately in Problem 6.12. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))

If you want the paper’s nearby equivalent reformulation, note that Section 6 presents the same issue as whether “admitting a norming M-basis” and “embedding into a Banach space with a norming M-basis” are distinct conditions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
refined_question: Is the class of Banach spaces admitting a norming Markushevich basis hereditary with respect to closed linear subspaces? Equivalently, if X is a Banach space that admits a norming Markushevich basis—i.e. a fundamental total biorthogonal system whose biorthogonal functionals span a norming subspace of X^*—and Z is a closed linear subspace of X, must Z, with the inherited norm, also admit a norming Markushevich basis? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
equivalent_formulation: Are the two properties “Y admits a norming Markushevich basis” and “Y embeds into a Banach space with a norming Markushevich basis” actually equivalent for Banach spaces Y? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s official heredity problem almost verbatim: Section 6 introduces the heredity problem, says it asks whether the existence of norming M-bases passes to subspaces, and then states this exactly as Problem 6.1. The nearby context needed to make the question self-contained is the paper’s definition of M-basis and norming M-basis in Section 2, Definition 2.1. Section 6 then immediately records the known positive cases: the separable case via Theorem 2.5 and the WLD-subspace case via Theorem 6.3, showing that the unrestricted version is the intended open problem. Finally, the paper separately isolates the complemented-subspace version as Problem 6.12, confirming that your draft correctly points to the broader Problem 6.1 and should not be narrowed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2402.18442))
